cross_cutting.evidence: printed_text prints whole only at or below PRINT_LIMIT=16,000 on every host. Every quoting packet in this group (test-strategy 43 KB, plan 80 KB, prepare 32 KB) prints a head, and _select_head drops QUOTED first. Across the run: 896 KB of quotes in 25 producer packets and 449 KB in 11 handoffs. The handoff quotes are the pre-stage text of files Improve then edits.
cross_cutting.proposal: Replace each quote with 'Read whole: HOME/<file> (<bytes>; sections: ...)'. For handoffs, add the bind-tree diff command. Keep the R-<n>/AD-<n> entry quotes (_entry_lines), which are small and item-specific.
cross_cutting.risk: MAIN TENET holds: every packet still names the file and requires a whole read. The loss is the frozen snapshot, which git keeps. Rule 2 favours it.

cross_cutting.pattern: In head mode, the guide paths, the original request, the delivery lines and the last-accepted summary are FILE_ONLY, so a printed head cites guides by label with no path.
cross_cutting.evidence: _producer_blocks puts _run_context_lines (STAGE_REFERENCES label:path, _run_rules with the request, delivery packet_lines) in 'run-context' FILE_ONLY. Six of seven producer packets in this group exceed 16 KB. Stage starts show bursts of read_file: discovery 10 in 31 s, test-strategy 8 in 42 s, prepare 8 in 67 s.
cross_cutting.proposal: (a) Move the STAGE_REFERENCES lines to a LOOKUP-tier block right after the duties. (b) After AX-1 and AX-3, raise PRINT_LIMIT to 20,000 (HEAD_LIMIT already is; Grok's measured whole-print bound), so discovery, research, spec, prepare and probably test-strategy print whole and need no file read.
cross_cutting.risk: PRINT_LIMIT also bounds where shiploop_status_hook.WINDOW (16,000) expects the status block. The status block sits in P0 near the top, so it stays inside the window. Re-run test/shiploop-head-order.test.py.

cross_cutting.pattern: The 5 KB original request is quoted in every producer packet and every Improve handoff.
cross_cutting.evidence: 125 KB across 25 producer packets and 51 KB across 11 handoffs. RUN/request.md already holds it with the S-index. Research, prepare and discovery used none of its text beyond what their predecessors' results and the Delivery exclusions line carry.
cross_cutting.proposal: Quote it whole at intake, spec and plan (the stages that map it). Elsewhere print one pointer line plus the Delivery exclusions line.
cross_cutting.risk: MAIN TENET: highest-value grounding text. Adopt only after one E2E run shows no scope drift. The exclusions line must keep every 'never' clause.

cross_cutting.pattern: The pointer line is stale and invites file reads for text the head already carries.
cross_cutting.evidence: Line 3: 'open it ... when this print was cut ... or you need the duties or the template'. Since 2026-10-16 the head carries duties and template as P0 (packet_head docstring).
cross_cutting.proposal: 'Full packet: <path>. Open it with a file tool only if this print lacks its last line === end ShipLoop head ===, or for what only the file holds: <list the FILE_ONLY blocks actually omitted>.'

cross_cutting.pattern: The 'ShipLoop navigator' prefix (owner question) and who reads it.
cross_cutting.evidence: The header line 'ShipLoop navigator | <stage> | revision N' is read by shiploop_status_hook.HEADER (the hook returns None unless stdout starts with it), the E2E harness (test/shiploop_e2e counters.py HEAD_START/HEADER, metrics.py PACKET_STAGE and KEPT_REPLY, flow.py HEAD, clear.py HEADER), shiploop-run-review export.py and template/index.html (the packet-head finder), and tests (shiploop_entry_recovery, shiploop_inner_state, shiploop-head-order, several more). The result heading '# ShipLoop navigator result' is ignored by shiploop_store.loads, which reads only the shiploop-state fence; only fixtures and test/shiploop-e2e-packet-anatomy.test.py ('result-contract') name it. The refusal prefix 'ShipLoop navigator: ' comes from shiploop_protocol.py main and is matched by test/shiploop_e2e/metrics.REFUSAL_LINE and the fidelity counters and tests.
cross_cutting.proposal: Drop '# ShipLoop navigator result' from the result template. It is safe for parsing, saves about 28 chars per packet, and needs a packet-anatomy test update. Keep the header line, or shorten it to 'ShipLoop | <stage> | revision N' only through one shared constant changed in lockstep across the status hook, the E2E regexes and run-review (about 10 chars per packet; low value). Keep the refusal prefix, or rename it to 'ShipLoop refused: ' with REFUSAL_LINE updated; it costs 20 chars per refusal and helps the model see the line came from ShipLoop.
cross_cutting.source: skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:_producer_blocks ('header'), improve_packet, the result template builder; shiploop_status_hook.py:HEADER; shiploop_protocol.py main; test/shiploop_e2e/*.py
cross_cutting.risk: The header is a parse anchor for the status hook. Removing it without updating HEADER silently stops the status display on every host.

cross_cutting.pattern: Each packet carries about 1 KB of low-value lines.
cross_cutting.evidence: Measured across the run's 25 producer packets: Last accepted transition 23.5 KB (truncated mid-word, e.g. 'static methods ' then '[truncated ...]', while the same result is listed under 'Results this stage builds on'); Recovery command repeated at the bottom 5.7 KB (line 2 already gives it); Consumer-delivery declarations 5.0 KB; obligations parenthetical 3.8 KB; Earlier-runs sentence 3.4 KB; Progress view line 2.7 KB (for the user; the model never opened it).
cross_cutting.proposal: Drop Last accepted for producer stages whose builds-on list names that result. Drop the bottom Recovery block (keep line 2). Apply A2-3, A2-4 and A1-3. Move Progress view into the narrative, which is for the user.
cross_cutting.risk: Last accepted is a re-grounding aid after compaction. The listed result file holds the whole summary, which removes the truncation's ambiguity, but only if the model opens it. Keep the block's one-line Stage/outcome header if that read is not trusted.

cross_cutting.pattern: Generic duties for service, MCP, async and JS-module concerns print on a platform and request that have none.
cross_cutting.evidence: Discovery items 9 and 11 (1.7 KB), research items 6 and 9, spec item 8, plan items 7, 12 and 13. The model either ignored them (research opened no guide) or wrote filler (plan's 'Module format: LWC ES modules').
cross_cutting.proposal: Gate them on request or intake words with the same mechanism as names_interactions. When a gate is off, print a one-line trigger plus guide.
